surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Farabee has a goal and two assists as the Flames take down the Red Wings
paras: Joel Farabee struck first for the Flames late in the first. It was a busy second period. Andrew Copp tied it up for Detroit early in the period, but the Red Wings didn’t score again. Zayne Parekh restored the Flames’ lead on the power play midway through the period. Ryan Strome and Matvei Gridin scored a minute and a half apart late in the period to stretch the lead to 4-1, and the Wings never had an answer. Ben Chiarot and Jake Middleton dropped the gloves late in the third. Farabee finished with a goal and two assists.

The score flatters the Flames: the Red Wings had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Red Wings win about six in ten. Devin Cooley made the difference in net, stopping 28 of 29. John Gibson stopped 21 of 25 for the Red Wings. The Flames improved to 4-6-0 and climbed to sixth in the Pacific, while the Red Wings fell to 4-4-3, seventh in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Red Wings’ six-game point streak is over.
Three straight wins for the Flames.
Zayne Parekh scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 16.
NHL.com had projected the Red Wings with 12 forwards and six defensemen, but they dressed 11 and seven.
